title: Texas Brisket
summary: Central Texas pit tradition — salt, pepper, smoke, time.
origins: German and Czech immigrants brought smoking traditions to Central Texas meat markets in the late 1800s. Brisket — a tough, cheap cut — became the icon after post-war barbecue joints standardized offset smokers and all-beef menus.
history: Aaron Franklin and the Austin barbecue boom (2000s–2010s) turned brisket into a national pilgrimage food. Purist rub is often just salt and coarse pepper (Dalmatian rub). Sauce on the side, if at all — the meat is the point.

timeline.event: Austin barbecue tourism globalizes brisket culture

teaching: Plan 1–1.5 hours per pound at 225–250°F — no shortcuts without quality loss.
Wrap at bark set (~165°F internal) in butcher paper, not foil, for Texas style.
Rest wrapped in cooler 1–4 hours — carryover tenderizes collagen.
fun_fact: Texas brisket was once a cheap cut smoked by immigrants — now people fly in for it.
